queries.hook: The wish to understand what these texts teach, and to find in them something steady to lean on.
queries.diagnose: The untrained mind runs like the wind, replaying and imagining; left to itself it becomes its own enemy.
queries.steady: The mind can be trained slowly, by practice and letting go; each time it wanders, it can be gently brought back.
queries.act: Bring the mind back each time it wanders, with practice and letting go; make the mind your friend through steady practice.
queries.story: A story of a student who came to a teacher with questions and was led, step by step, toward the truth.

hook.speaker: Rama
hook.setting: After the war, Lakshmana finds Rama alone and asks how to cross the sea of confusion.
hook.sanskrit: एवं सदा जातपरात्मभावनः स्वानन्दतुष्टः परिविस्मृताखिलः । आस्ते स नित्यात्मसुखप्रकाशकः साक्षाद्विमुक्तोऽचलवारिसिन्धुवत् ॥
hook.line: Content in an inner joy, he becomes like an ocean of still water.
hook.translation: Always absorbed in the sense of the supreme Self, content in his own joy and forgetting all else, he lives radiating that inner happiness, free, like an ocean of still water.

words.en: one who contemplates the supreme self

hook.why: Quiet sitting and steady faith carry you until understanding becomes natural.

prasang.title: Sit quietly, keep faith
prasang.summary: Rama describes sitting in a quiet place with the senses at rest until the mind becomes like a still ocean, and tells Lakshmana that until he sees the divine everywhere, devotion keeps it alive in the heart.
prasang.lesson: Quiet sitting and steady faith carry you until understanding becomes natural.

hook.for_you: You are here to read, and your calm focus is already a kind of answer.

alternates.speaker: Bhartrihari
alternates.setting: From 'Worship of Shiva': gratitude for a simple life.
alternates.sanskrit: यदेतत्स्वच्छन्दं विहरणमकार्पण्यमशनं सहार्यैः संवासः श्रुतमुपशमैकव्रतफलम् । मनो मन्दस्पन्दं बहिरपि चिरस्यापि विमृशन् न जाने कस्यैष परिणतिरुदारस्य तपसः ॥
alternates.line: Freedom, simple food, good company, learning that brings calm: what did I do to deserve this?
alternates.translation: This freedom to wander at will, food eaten without humiliation, living among noble people, learning whose only fruit is calm, a mind that stirs only gently even when it looks outward for long: I do not know what generous austerity this is the fruit of.
alternates.why: Gratitude for a simple life, and devotion without rivalry between forms of God.

prasang.title: Vairagyashatakam: Worship of Shiva
prasang.summary: Devotional verses longing for a quiet life by the Ganga in Shiva's presence, including a famous non-sectarian line that Shiva and Vishnu are one in essence.
prasang.lesson: Gratitude for a simple life, and devotion without rivalry between forms of God.

alternates.speaker: Krishna
alternates.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on why even the fulfilled keep working for the world.
alternates.sanskrit: यस्त्वात्मरतिरेव स्यादात्मतृप्तश्च मानवः । आत्मन्येव च सन्तुष्टस्तस्य कार्यं न विद्यते ॥
alternates.line: One who is content and delighted in their own self has nothing left to prove.
alternates.translation: But for the person who delights only in the self, is satisfied with the self, and content in the self alone, there is nothing that must be done.
alternates.why: People copy what you do, not what you say; keep showing up.

prasang.title: Even the wise, even God, act for the world's sake
prasang.summary: The one content in the self has nothing left to gain, yet the wise, like Janaka and Krishna himself, keep working because others follow their example.
prasang.lesson: People copy what you do, not what you say; keep showing up.

verse.speaker: Yama
verse.setting: Yama's chariot image of the human being.
verse.sanskrit: आत्मानँ रथितं विद्धि शरीरँ रथमेव तु । बुद्धिं तु सारथिं विद्धि मनः प्रग्रहमेव च ॥ इन्द्रियाणि हयानाहुर्विषयांस्तेषु गोचरान् । आत्मेन्द्रिय मनोयुक्त भोक्तेत्याहुर्मनीषिणः ॥
verse.line: You are the rider, your body the chariot, your intellect the driver, your mind the reins.
verse.translation: Know the self as the rider, the body as the chariot, the intellect as the charioteer and the mind as the reins. The senses, they say, are the horses, and the things of the world are the roads they run on.
verse.why: Hold the reins of your mind, or your senses will drive for you.

prasang.title: The chariot of the self
prasang.summary: Yama pictures a person as a chariot: the self is the rider, the body the chariot, the intellect the driver, the mind the reins and the senses the horses. With a steady mind the horses obey; without it they bolt. He ends with the call to arise and wake.
prasang.lesson: Hold the reins of your mind, or your senses will drive for you.

why: a runaway mind is horses without a hand on the reins; it can be driven

verse.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
verse.setting: Poem 'Peace', composed at Ridgely Manor, New York, 1899.
verse.line: The silence between speaking; Between two fits of passion — It is the calm of heart.
verse.translation: It is sweet rest in music; And pause in sacred art; The silence between speaking; Between two fits of passion — It is the calm of heart.

verse.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
verse.setting: Karma-Yoga classes, New York, 1895–96, end of chapter 1: the ideal worker.
verse.line: in the midst of the intensest activity finds the silence and solitude of the desert.
verse.translation: The ideal man is he who, in the midst of the greatest silence and solitude, finds the intensest activity, and in the midst of the intensest activity finds the silence and solitude of the desert. He has learnt the secret of restraint, he has controlled himself. He goes through the streets of a big city with all its traffic, and his mind is as calm as if he were in a cave, where not a sound could reach him; and he is intensely working all the time.
verse.why: Character is built in ordinary actions, and you are building it right now.

prasang.title: Karma-Yoga 1: how work makes character
prasang.summary: He defines karma as work and says character is the sum of the impressions our actions leave. Misery teaches as much as joy, and character shows in small daily actions, not big moments. The ideal worker finds calm in the middle of intense activity.
prasang.lesson: Character is built in ordinary actions, and you are building it right now.

verse.speaker: Ribhu
verse.setting: Ribhu begins his answer to Nidagha.
verse.sanskrit: मोक्षद्वारे द्वारपालश्चत्वारः परिकीर्तिताः । शमो विचारः सन्तोषश्चतुर्थः साधुसङ्गमः ॥ एकं वा सर्वयत्नेन सर्वमुत्सृज्य संश्रयेत् । एकस्मिन्वशगे यान्ति चत्वारोऽपि वशं गताः ॥
verse.line: Freedom has four gatekeepers: calm, inquiry, contentment and good company. Win one, and the others follow.
verse.translation: Four gatekeepers are named at the door of freedom: calm, inquiry, contentment, and the company of good people. Take refuge in even one of them with full effort, setting all else aside; when one is won, all four come under your control.
verse.why: Start with calm or contentment, and the rest follows.

prasang.title: Ribhu on calm and contentment
prasang.summary: Ribhu answers Nidagha: freedom has four gatekeepers (calm, inquiry, contentment and good company), and winning one brings the rest. In a calm mind sorrow and anxiety vanish; restlessness is simply the mind's nature, and only your own mind can lift you out.
prasang.lesson: Start with calm or contentment, and the rest follows.

why: inquiry is one of the four

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna's final counsel: act with devotion, reflect, choose, and take refuge.
verse.sanskrit: इति ते ज्ञानमाख्यातं गुह्याद्गुह्यतरं मया । विमृश्यैतदशेषेण यथेच्छसि तथा कुरु ॥
verse.line: I've told you all I know. Reflect on it fully, then do as you choose.
verse.translation: Thus I have declared to you this knowledge, more secret than all secrets. Reflect on it fully, and then do as you wish.
verse.why: Reflect fully, choose freely, and set down the fear.

prasang.title: Action with devotion: surrender
prasang.summary: Krishna urges Arjuna to offer all action, warns that ego will only trip him, tells him to reflect fully and then choose, and finally to take refuge in him alone and not grieve.
prasang.lesson: Reflect fully, choose freely, and set down the fear.

why: full reflection before acting is the instruction
Reflect fully, then decide and begin.

story.title: Janaka's songs of simple happiness
story.summary: In three short chapters Janaka describes how he has become calm: tired of busy body, speech and thought, he no longer renounces or grabs, and simply does what comes and lives happily.
story.lesson: Happiness can be simple: do what comes, stop both grabbing and renouncing.
